Insight 01 · Autonomous navigation & SLAM

Optimized UAV Localization & Autonomous Navigation for Tightly Closed Industrial Spaces

Robin Havås et al. · University of Agder, Norway
Goal

Build a UAV navigation stack for precise localization and cost-effective autonomy in GPS-denied industrial spaces.

Challenge

Industrial inspection/surveillance needs navigation without GPS, using affordable off-the-shelf components.

Method
  • Integrate SLAM with obstacle detection / avoidance and real-time performance
  • Use off-the-shelf sensors, edge devices and UAV control
  • Test in ROS + Gazebo with an IRIS 3DR drone across environments
Novelty

A cost-effective, off-the-shelf navigation stack tuned for GPS-denied industrial inspection.

Impact

Enables automated inspection in Industry-4.0 settings without costly infrastructure.

[1] R. Havås et al., “Optimized UAV Localization and Autonomous Navigation Stack for Tightly Closed Industrial Spaces,” IEEE SysCon 2024.
Insight 02 · Autonomous navigation & SLAM

AUV Kalman-Filter Trajectory Estimation from Acoustic + Inertial Sensors

Juan de França Silva et al. · Instituto Tecnológico de Aeronáutica, Brazil
Goal

Estimate AUV trajectories accurately in confined underwater spaces such as tunnels.

Challenge

Acoustic positioning fails in confined spaces due to reflections and scattering, so AUVs rely on internal sensors.

Method
  • Fuse DVL, IMU, magnetometer and depth sensor with a Kalman Filter
  • Validate in confined tunnels and autonomous dam inspections
  • Compare against GPS-RTK and dead-reckoning trajectories
Novelty

A KF sensor fusion that significantly beats dead reckoning for confined-space AUVs.

Impact

Reliable underwater inspection (dams, tunnels) where acoustic / GPS positioning is unavailable.

[2] J. de França Silva et al., “AUV Kalman Filter-Based Trajectory Estimation Using Acoustic and Inertial Sensors,” IEEE SysCon 2024.
Insight 03 · Autonomous navigation & SLAM

3D EKF-SLAM Using Cylindrical & Planar Features with Multilevel Mapping

Leonardo Mariga et al. · Aeronautics Institute of Technology, Brazil
Goal

Build accurate 3D maps for mobile robots using geometric features.

Challenge

3D SLAM must robustly extract and match features for localization in real environments.

Method
  • RGBD camera; RANSAC for planes and DBSCAN for cylinders within an EKF
  • Hessian-normal-form planes + centroid-radius cylinders; Mahalanobis matching
  • Simulate in ROS / Gazebo; real tests with the Omni robot
Novelty

Combines planar and cylindrical features with multilevel mapping in EKF-SLAM.

Impact

Better structured-environment mapping for domestic, exploration and surveillance robots.

[3] L. Mariga et al., “3D EKF-SLAM Using Cylindrical and Planar Features With Multilevel Mapping Representation,” IEEE SysCon 2024.
Insight 04 · Autonomous planning, routing & safety

Constant-Time-Delay Leader Following for Wheeled Robots (Uncertainty-Tuned MPC)

Kai Wang et al. · Queen's University, Canada
Goal

Let a follower robot trail a leader's path at a fixed time delay (e.g. military convoys).

Challenge

The follower must reconstruct and track the leader's past trajectory despite uncertainty.

Method
  • Estimate a sequence of leader waypoints
  • Bridge estimator and controller with a model predictive controller (MPC)
  • Tune the MPC for uncertainty in the estimated waypoints
Novelty

An uncertainty-tuned MPC coupling a waypoint estimator to a constant-delay follower.

Impact

Validated indoors with acceptable position/velocity error — practical convoying.

[4] K. Wang et al., “Monkey See, Monkey Do: Constant Time Delay Leader Following for Wheeled Mobile Robots using Uncertainty-Tuned MPC,” IEEE SysCon 2024.
Insight 05 · Autonomous planning, routing & safety

Graph Neural Network for Dynamic Emergency-Vehicle Routing

Jean-Alexis Delamer et al. · St. Francis Xavier University, Canada
Goal

Reduce emergency-vehicle response time to traffic accidents.

Challenge

Routing must adapt dynamically to changing accident and traffic conditions.

Method
  • Deep RL with PPO and a graph attention network
  • Model as a Dynamic Travelling Repairman Problem (an MDP)
  • Use probabilistic accident models from Toronto / Halifax open data
Novelty

An MDP + graph-attention formulation of dynamic emergency-vehicle routing.

Impact

Faster emergency response — directly life-saving.

[5] J.-A. Delamer et al., “Graph Neural Network to Solve the Dynamic Emergency Vehicles Routing Problems,” IEEE SysCon 2024.
Insight 06 · Autonomous planning, routing & safety

Optimal Path Generation & Real-time Scheduling for Autonomous Mobile Platforms

Abdullah Rasul et al. · OntarioTech University, Canada
Goal

Plan and schedule routes for autonomous sweeping trucks, including breakdown scenarios.

Challenge

Routes must be re-planned in real time when a vehicle breaks down.

Method
  • Model as a Capacitated Arc Routing Problem (CARP)
  • Cluster-first / optimize-second: spectral clustering + TSP with simulated annealing
  • Real-time breakdown handling via Kernighan-Lin bisection and Dijkstra reconnection
Novelty

Combines CARP, clustering and real-time edge redistribution for resilient routing.

Impact

Seamless autonomous street-sweeping that recovers from breakdowns.

[6] A. Rasul et al., “Optimal Path Generation and Real-time Scheduling for Autonomous Mobile Platforms,” IEEE SysCon 2024.
Insight 07 · Autonomous planning, routing & safety

On-Demand Triple Modular Redundancy for Automotive Applications

Martin J. Stoffel et al. · Karlsruhe Institute of Technology, Germany
Goal

Achieve fail-operational autonomy without a human fallback.

Challenge

AVs need high reliability / availability; >500M lines of code and ISO 26262 leave technical redundancy open.

Method
  • On-demand TMR: redundant apps across multiple ECUs
  • Fail-silent architecture on service-oriented ECUs with ROS2 Galactic
  • Inspired by avionic redundancy; use-cases from AV sensors and data rates
Novelty

Redundancy applied on-demand to minimize overhead in a fail-operational E/E architecture.

Impact

A path to auto-recovery in automated driving without manual takeover.

[7] M. J. Stoffel et al., “On-Demand Triple Modular Redundancy for Automotive Applications,” IEEE SysCon 2024.
Insight 08 · Autonomous planning, routing & safety

Safeguarding Autonomous UAV Navigation with Evolving Behavior Trees

N. Potteiger & X. Koutsoukos · Vanderbilt University, USA
Goal

Ensure safe autonomous UAV navigation in dynamic environments.

Challenge

Learning-enabled components must handle dynamics while guaranteeing safety.

Method
  • Evolving Behavior Trees (EBTs) with explicit safety components
  • Automated EBT construction via genetic programming
  • Optimize learning components with hierarchical RL; safe transfer to new environments
Novelty

Safe-by-design EBTs combining genetic-programming structure search with hierarchical RL.

Impact

Collision-free UAV missions that transfer to unseen environments.

[8] N. Potteiger & X. Koutsoukos, “Safeguarding Autonomous UAV Navigation: Agent Design using Evolving Behavior Trees,” IEEE SysCon 2024.
Insight 09 · Autonomous planning, routing & safety

Autonomous Vehicle Development as a System of Systems

A. Elhadeedy & J. Daily · Colorado State University, USA
Goal

Coordinate AV development across many vendors as a System of Systems (SoS).

Challenge

Disparate global vendors cause coordination errors across perception, decision, control and comms.

Method
  • A tailored SoS model integrating safety + security and feedback loops
  • Compare Named Data Networking (NDN) vs SOME/IP for communication
  • A queuing model for certificate authentication at scale
Novelty

SoS governance for AV constituent systems, with NDN security advantages at scale.

Impact

Fewer integration errors and stronger security in multi-vendor AV programs.

[9] A. Elhadeedy & J. Daily, “Autonomous Vehicle Development as a System of Systems and Constituent Systems Networking,” IEEE SysCon 2024.
Insight 10 · Prediction, AI & neuromorphic

Vehicle Trajectory Prediction with Deep Learning for ADAS & AVs

Shehab Alsanwy et al. · Deakin University, Australia
Goal

Predict vehicle trajectories for collision avoidance and path planning.

Challenge

Traditional models ignore driver-behavior variability (especially braking), hurting accuracy.

Method
  • LSTM and GRU networks
  • Incorporate driver braking patterns plus vehicle dynamics
  • Evaluate with RMSE / MAE
Novelty

Adding braking patterns markedly improves prediction; LSTM beats GRU.

Impact

More accurate ADAS / AV trajectory prediction and safer driving.

[10] S. Alsanwy et al., “Vehicle Trajectory Prediction Using Deep Learning for ADAS and Autonomous Vehicles,” IEEE SysCon 2024.
Insight 11 · Prediction, AI & neuromorphic

Deep RL Agents for Decision Making in Cooperative Gameplay

J. Heaton & S. Givigi · Queen's University, Canada
Goal

Build cooperative AI agents for the tower-building game Menara, to help children with disabilities.

Challenge

Agents must make good pillar / tile placement decisions under uncertainty.

Method
  • RL (Q-learning, deep Q, soft actor-critic) per decision type
  • Separate agents for pillar vs tile placement, trained independently
  • Simplified tower mechanics for training
Novelty

Decomposed cooperative-game agents trained independently per decision.

Impact

Tile agent 62% / pillar agent 88% success — toward assistive cooperative play.

[11] J. Heaton & S. Givigi, “Deep Reinforcement Learning Agents for Decision Making for Gameplay,” IEEE SysCon 2024.
Insight 12 · Prediction, AI & neuromorphic

3D Convolutional Spiking Neural Network for Human Action Recognition

T. Mohottalalage & H. Leung · University of Calgary, Canada
Goal

Energy-efficient video action recognition.

Challenge

3D CNNs are accurate but memory- and compute-heavy.

Method
  • A 3D Convolutional Spiking NN with Leaky-Integrate-and-Fire neurons
  • Modulating STDP supervised learning via global error feedback
  • Two 3D convolutional layers + two spiking layers
Novelty

A supervised-STDP spiking CNN competitive with 3D CNNs at far lower power and memory.

Impact

Real-time, low-power action recognition for edge video analysis.

[12] T. M. N. B. Mohottalalage & H. Leung, “3D Convolutional Spiking Neural Network for Human Action Recognition Using Modulating STDP With Global Error Feedback,” IEEE SysCon 2024.
Insight 13 · Digital twins & MBSE

Trainee Perspectives on VR Environments with Haptic Feedback

O. K. Xanthidou et al. · Brunel University London, UK
Goal

Evaluate adaptable haptic feedback in single-user VR training environments.

Challenge

Understand how haptic vibrations affect immersion and learning.

Method
  • A trainee study in standard classroom settings
  • Tasks involving haptic feedback
  • Non-probability sampling
Novelty

Trainee-centered evidence that haptic feedback enhances immersive VR training.

Impact

Guidance for designing effective VR / haptic education.

[13] O. K. Xanthidou et al., “Investigating Trainee Perspectives on Virtual Reality Environments with Haptic Feedback,” IEEE SysCon 2024.
Insight 14 · Digital twins & MBSE

Next-Generation Digital-Twin Robotic Frameworks for Cyber-Human-Physical Contexts

Joe Cecil · Oklahoma State University, USA
Goal

Link cyber, human and physical facets with 3D digital twins and VR / MR.

Challenge

Advanced robots (lunar missions, rehab cobots) need training, layout and immersive analysis.

Method
  • 3D digital twins for training and layout modification
  • Cobot applications with safety / efficiency control
  • Support Cyber-Physical Systems and Industry 4.0
Novelty

Next-gen digital-twin frameworks spanning cyber-human-physical robotics.

Impact

Better cobot support, including automated mobility aids for challenged individuals.

[14] J. Cecil, “Emergence of Next-generation Digital Twin based Robotic Frameworks for Cyber-Human-Physical Contexts,” IEEE SysCon 2024.
Insight 15 · Digital twins & MBSE

Model-Driven Cloud-Based Healthcare App Using Colored Petri Nets

A. Cagaanan & V. Gehlot · Villanova University, USA
Goal

Improve software quality during cloud integration of consumer-oriented apps.

Challenge

Cloud adoption rushes features, risking security, performance and standards.

Method
  • A model-driven approach with Colored Petri Nets (CPNs) for design-implementation harmony
  • A cloud-based healthcare app for verification and prototyping
  • ML integration in the simulations
Novelty

CPN-based model-driven development that bridges design and implementation.

Impact

Higher-quality, adaptable cloud software via up-front formal design.

[15] A. Cagaanan & V. Gehlot, “Model-Driven System Development for a Cloud-Based Healthcare Application Using Colored Petri Nets,” IEEE SysCon 2024.
Insight 16 · Digital twins & MBSE

Towards Automating MBSE in Industry — An Experience Report

Johan Cederbladh et al. · Mälardalen University, Sweden (+ EU partners)
Goal

Automate Cyber-Physical-System design by combining MBSE, DevOps and AI.

Challenge

CPS design is hard (heterogeneity, concurrency, timing); plus CAEX interoperability, legacy artifacts and the academia–industry gap.

Method
  • Prescriptive modeling with model transformations and views
  • Modeling-process mining
  • AI-based modeling recommendations
Novelty

An industry experience report on automating MBSE end-to-end.

Impact

A practical path to adopting automated MBSE in industry.

[16] J. Cederbladh et al., “Towards Automating Model-Based Systems Engineering in Industry — An Experience Report,” IEEE SysCon 2024.
Insight 17 · Digital twins & MBSE

MBSE for eVTOL Development in Air-Ambulance Service

Yue Liu et al. · COMAC, China; ISAE-SUPAERO, France
Goal

Apply MBSE to develop an eVTOL air-ambulance for Urban Air Mobility (UAM).

Challenge

eVTOL EMS development has integration, spatial and payload complexities.

Method
  • MBSE with UML, Drawio and Capella
  • Three phases: conceptual, system and architecture design
  • A case study for patient + equipment transport
Novelty

An end-to-end MBSE case study for eVTOL air ambulances.

Impact

Stakeholder-aligned eVTOL EMS design and lessons for UAM.

[17] Y. Liu et al., “Application of MBSE Approach in eVTOL Development for Air Ambulance Service,” IEEE SysCon 2024.
Conclusions

Synthesis across the papers

Insights

  • Autonomous systems dominate the program — localization / SLAM, routing, redundancy / safety and trajectory prediction.
  • Learning is pervasive but safety-framed: RL, graph networks and behavior trees are paired with redundancy, verification and uncertainty tuning.
  • MBSE is maturing from notation to automation — Colored Petri Nets, Capella/UML workflows and AI-assisted modeling.

Vision

  • Fail-operational autonomy without a human fallback (on-demand redundancy, safe-by-design behavior trees).
  • Digital twins linking cyber, human and physical systems for training and control.
  • Energy-efficient, neuromorphic AI (spiking networks) for real-time edge perception.

Implications for us

  • Treat autonomy as a System of Systems — coordinate multi-vendor constituents with integrated safety and security.
  • Adopt model-driven / MBSE practices (CPN, Capella) to raise software quality and shorten CPS design.
  • Invest in GPS-denied localization and uncertainty-aware planning for real industrial and emergency use.
